TASK: T1 - failing tests for the user-level Arbiter hook (RED, test-first).

Worktree: {worktree}
Prior results: {prior_results}

Background. The Kyber Arbiter is a hook that gates agent dispatches. The user-level (global) Claude hook runs `kyber-weave-arbiter hook --harness claude --scope global`. Today `HookCommand.Run` (src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/HookCommand.cs) defers whenever the project's `.kyber-weave/kyber-weave.yml` sets `arbiter.enabled` (true or false) and logs `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project.` - so a project with no project Claude hook is never gated. The fix (implemented later by another worker, task T4) is:
- The user-level hook EVALUATES under the project's configuration when no project hook covers the dispatch. It writes the ledger and decision log to `<project>/artifacts/arbiter/` exactly as a project-scope hook would, and logs `Arbiter global scope: evaluating under the project configuration.` The case with no project config is unchanged (user config, ledger under `<home>/.kyber-weave/arbiter/projects/<root-key>/`).
- It still defers on an explicit `arbiter.enabled: false`, logging `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (project opts out: arbiter.enabled: false).`
- Other harnesses keep deferring, logging `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (<harness>: no per-dispatch probe; the project's own <harness> hooks decide).`
- Candidate project hooks for Claude: `<project>/.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`; the effective agent file for the payload's `agent_type` (project `.claude/agents/<agent_type>.md`, else `<home>/.claude/agents/<agent_type>.md`; `agent_type` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` or no agent file is used); every effective skill (`<home>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` shadows `<project>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`). A source counts only when its hooks have the event's exact container (`PreToolUse` or `PostToolUse`) with an entry whose matcher matches `Agent`/`Task` and whose command runs `kyber-weave-arbiter hook --harness claude` without `--scope global`.
- One evaluation per dispatch via a claim file `<project>/artifacts/arbiter/claims/<tool_use_id>.pre` (or `.post`) created with CreateNew and holding the single line `project` or `global`. Only Agent/Task dispatch events claim. The project-scope hook claims `project` before evaluating; if a `global` claim already exists it allows silently and logs `Arbiter: dispatch already claimed by the global hook; not evaluated twice.`; an existing `project` claim does not stop it (two project hooks behave as today). The user-level hook: no candidates -> claim `global` and evaluate at once; candidates -> poll for any claim every 50 ms up to 1500 ms; claim appears -> defer, logging `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (claimed by <source>).`; none -> claim `global`, evaluate, and log which candidates did not fire.
- Unmarked dispatch behaviour is unchanged: `Explore` passes through silently; an unmarked `architect` dispatch is denied by `KW-ARB-PLANNER-001`.

TASK: T2 - failing tests for per-harness gating in `arbiter doctor` and `arbiter status` (RED, test-first).

Worktree: {worktree}
Prior results: {prior_results}

Background. `kyber-weave arbiter doctor` prints `ok Project hooks: installed.` whenever any harness has a project deployment, and `arbiter status` prints `project overrides global`; both hid a Claude project that nothing gated. The fix (task T5, another worker) adds a shared helper that lists every INSTALLED harness and prints one line per harness with its gating state and fix command:
- Installed means: in `arbiter.global.targets` of `<home>/.kyber-weave/kyber-weave.yml`; or owning an Arbiter hook in the global Squad receipt (a receipt hook BLOCK, or the harness's own shim hook file such as Copilot's `hooks/kyber-arbiter.json`; ordinary agent and skill files never count); or with a project Arbiter deployment.
- States: `gated by project hooks` (Claude names its project sources, e.g. `.claude/agents/csharp-dev.md`); `gated by the global hook under this project's configuration` (Claude only, when the user-level hook is installed and live); `gated by the global hook under your user configuration` (no project Arbiter config); `opted out` (project `arbiter.enabled: false`); `fallback-only` (Warp, ZCode: no hook, no fix, no diagnostic); or `ungated` with the fix command.
- Claude's user-level hook counts as installed only when `hooks.PreToolUse` (exact case) in the global `settings.json` holds an entry with matcher `^(Agent|Task)$` and command `kyber-weave-arbiter hook --harness claude --scope global`; an entry only under lower-case `hooks.preToolUse` does not count.
- Fix commands: Claude `kyber-weave arbiter install --target claude`; any other harness `kyber-weave arbiter install --project --target <token>`.
- Diagnostics: `KW-ARB-PROJECT-001` (warning) once per ungated harness, naming it; new `KW-ARB-GLOBAL-001` (warning) for a global receipt hook block or shim hook file whose harness is missing from `arbiter.global.targets`, hint `kyber-weave arbiter install --target <token>`.
- The text `Project hooks: installed`, `ungated by design` and `project overrides global` disappear.

Background. `SquadHookJsonBlock` (src/KyberWeave.Core.Squad/Deployment/SquadHookJsonBlock.cs) splices Squad's Arbiter hook entries into shared hook files. For both the Cursor and Claude formats it routes through `CursorArrays`, which keeps a lower-case container name (`preToolUse`, `postToolUse`) unless the PascalCase key already exists, so a Claude `settings.json` gets lower-case names. Claude Code documents only `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse`. The fix (task T6, another worker): for `SquadHookBlockFormat.Claude` only, always write `hooks.PreToolUse` / `hooks.PostToolUse`; on splice remove Squad entries from both spellings and delete a lower-case container the removal emptied, leaving one that still holds user entries; `RemoveContent` removes Squad entries from both spellings and keeps user entries; `FindDrift` treats `/hooks/preToolUse` and `/hooks/PreToolUse` (and the post pair) as one container when re-anchoring. Cursor stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

TASK: T4 - the user-level Arbiter hook evaluates Claude dispatches unless a project hook covers them (GREEN).

Worktree: {worktree}
Prior results (T1's RED tests and evidence): {prior_results}

Goal: make `KyberWeave.Tests.ArbiterGlobalHookCoverageTests` and `KyberWeave.Tests.ArbiterGlobalHookRuntimeTests` pass unchanged. Do not edit any test.

Behaviour to implement:
1. Deferral rule. Under `HookScope.Global` the hook defers only when (a) the project config sets `arbiter.enabled: false` explicitly - log `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (project opts out: arbiter.enabled: false).`; or (b) the adapter offers no coverage probe (every harness except Claude) and the project enables Arbiter - log `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (<harness>: no per-dispatch probe; the project's own <harness> hooks decide).`; or (c) Claude's claim logic below says a project hook has it. A project with no config, or one that does not set `arbiter.enabled`, keeps today's user-config path and home ledger.
2. Evaluating under the project's configuration. When Claude's user-level hook evaluates for an enabled project, it uses the project config and builds the `HookContext` with `HookScope.Project`, so `ArbiterHookDecisionEngine.ResolveArbiterDirectory` picks `<project>/artifacts/arbiter/` (ledger, decision log, in-flight ledger, git-facts snapshots) and providers resolve as for a project hook. Log `Arbiter global scope: evaluating under the project configuration.` Change no provider, model or key handling; never print a key.
3. Coverage probe (new public static class `ClaudeHookCoverage` in namespace KyberWeave.Core.Arbiter, file src/KyberWeave.Core/Arbiter/ClaudeHookCoverage.cs, with `///` docs): `IReadOnlyList<string> CandidateSources(string projectRoot, string homeDirectory, string? agentType, string eventName, string toolName)` returns the relative paths of hook definitions that would fire: `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` under the project (JSON `hooks`); when `agentType` matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$`, the effective agent file (project `.claude/agents/<agentType>.md`, else `<home>/.claude/agents/<agentType>.md`; YAML frontmatter `hooks`); every effective skill (for each name under `<project>/.claude/skills/` and `<home>/.claude/skills/`, the personal `SKILL.md` when both exist). A source counts only when its hooks map has the exact container named by `eventName` (`PreToolUse` or `PostToolUse`) holding an entry whose `matcher` (a .NET regex, 100 ms timeout; compile failure or timeout = no match) matches `toolName`, and whose hook command contains `kyber-weave-arbiter hook --harness claude` and not `--scope global`. Unreadable or malformed files are skipped; nothing throws. Also expose what the doctor (task T5) needs to list the project's sources without an agent type.
4. Claims (new internal static class `DispatchClaim`, file src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/DispatchClaim.cs): the claim is `<project>/artifacts/arbiter/claims/<id>.<pre|post>`, where `<id>` is the payload's `tool_use_id` when it matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`, else its lower-case SHA-256 hex; created with `FileMode.CreateNew`; content one line, `project` or `global`. TryClaim also deletes claim files older than 24 hours in that folder. ReadOwner returns the existing line. WaitForClaim polls every 50 ms for up to 1500 ms.
5. Adapter seam: add two default interface members to `IHarnessHookAdapter` (src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/IHarnessHookAdapter.cs) returning null - one for the candidate sources of a payload (given repo root and home), one for its claim key (`tool_use_id` plus `pre`/`post`), non-null only for Agent/Task dispatch events. `ClaudeHookAdapter` (src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/Adapters/ClaudeHookAdapter.cs) implements both through `ClaudeHookCoverage`, reading `agent_type`, `tool_name` and `hook_event_name`.
6. `HookCommand.Run` (src/KyberWeave.Arbiter/Hooks/HookCommand.cs) replaces `IsGlobalScopeProjectDefer`. Project scope: for a dispatch event with a claim key and an enabled config, TryClaim `project` before `adapter.Handle`; if the file exists and holds `global`, allow silently (write the adapter's `DisabledAllowDocument` if any) and log `Arbiter: dispatch already claimed by the global hook; not evaluated twice.`; otherwise evaluate as today. User-level Claude: no candidates -> TryClaim `global` and evaluate; candidates -> WaitForClaim; a claim appears -> defer, logging `Arbiter global scope: deferred-to-project (claimed by <first candidate source>).`; none -> TryClaim `global` (a lost race defers the same way) and evaluate, logging which candidates did not fire. No `tool_use_id`: candidates -> defer naming them; none -> evaluate.
7. Keep unmarked-dispatch behaviour: `Explore` passes through; unmarked `architect` is denied by `KW-ARB-PLANNER-001`.
